storyboard.claim: The lightbulb-in-an-empty-room image is the myth of the solitary genius.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A light bulb switching on over the host in a bare room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the chunk on the popular image of creativity.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the myth the next beats will complicate.
storyboard.staging: Host with a knowing smirk beside the light bulb: the classic myth, half-mocked.

storyboard.claim: Creativity is a social process of finding hidden problems.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host studies a magnifier, searching for something unseen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Breaks the lightbulb myth with the opposite claim.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces problem finding as the social core, with the astronomer Vera Rubin as the example.
storyboard.staging: Host thinking over a magnifier: the search for hidden problems.

storyboard.claim: Vera Rubin works alone in a dim lab in the late 1980s.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dark room silhouette lit only by a glowing screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the astronomer example a place and a time.
storyboard.addedInformation: The screen glow is the only light: the lab is dark, the work is hard.
storyboard.staging: Silhouetted figure at a dim lab, lit by a screen, studying spectral data.

storyboard.claim: Physics predicted outer stars should orbit more slowly than inner ones.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host explaining the expected orbit speeds.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the expectation Rubin's data will break.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the textbook expectation clearly before the data contradicts it.
storyboard.staging: Host talking, neutral, presenting the expected rule.

storyboard.claim: The expectation matches how planets orbit the sun, which makes it feel right.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host gesturing toward the familiar solar-system comparison.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the expectation feels obvious.
storyboard.addedInformation: The solar-system analogy is why the expectation seems intuitive.
storyboard.staging: Host talking evenly: this is the reasoning everyone accepts.

storyboard.claim: The data forces an uncomfortable conclusion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host holding notes, looking shaken by the numbers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from expectation to the data.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the moment the numbers stop fitting the expectation.
storyboard.staging: Host with a fearful face and thinking pose over the notes: the data is alarming.

storyboard.claim: Outer stars move much faster than expected.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host reacting, surprised, while describing the fast stars.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the anomaly that the next beat explains.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the galaxy should fly apart at that speed.
storyboard.staging: Host surprised at the speed: the anomaly is the claim.

storyboard.claim: Fast outer stars would fly apart unless invisible matter holds the galaxy together.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow: fast stars, galaxy flies apart, invisible matter.
storyboard.onScreenText: Fast stars, flies apart, invisible matter
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the anomaly from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the cause-effect chain that leads to dark matter.
storyboard.staging: Diagram beat: the reasoning chain carries the claim, host thinking.

storyboard.claim: The moment feels like a solitary flash of insight, the myth again.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lone silhouette in a dark room, thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the solitary-genius image while the data is still private.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the myth as Rubin experienced it in that single moment.
storyboard.staging: Lone silhouette in a dark room: the solitary figure the narration is describing.

storyboard.claim: The insight rests on years of hard data and hostile colleagues.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The gatekeeper stands at the panel room, pointing, sharp and hostile.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the social cost behind the lone moment.
storyboard.addedInformation: The panel room stands in for the field that doubts the discovery.
storyboard.staging: Gatekeeper with an angry, confrontational face: the threat of colleagues' skepticism.

storyboard.claim: You must locate the right problem before you can solve it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host pointing with a magnifier at the problem.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the story into a rule about problem finding.
storyboard.addedInformation: Problem finding is named as a social, systemic act.
storyboard.staging: Host pointing with a magnifier: find the problem before solving it.

callout.text: Nobody can be anybody without somebody

storyboard.claim: John Wheeler's quote: identity depends on other people being around.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host talking, quoting Wheeler.
storyboard.onScreenText: Nobody can be anybody without somebody
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces Wheeler as the authority on social thinking.
storyboard.addedInformation: The quote is the narrator's own words, verbatim.
storyboard.staging: Host talking evenly: the quote carries the claim.

storyboard.claim: Ideas must be tested against the field to see what echoes back.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boy scientist pointing an idea at the gatekeeper, who listens.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the field a concrete listener.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gatekeeper stands for the field that gives feedback.
storyboard.staging: Boy pointing toward the skeptical panel: his idea goes to the field.

storyboard.claim: Without colleagues you lose your sense of which problems matter.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A compass icon beside the host talking about the faculty lounge.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the cost of isolation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Bearing means direction: the compass shows the lost direction of problems.
storyboard.staging: Compass icon with host talking: direction is lost without the field.

storyboard.claim: You can waste years on a problem the field no longer cares about.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass beside the host slumped with worry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the time cost of isolation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hourglass shows the time running out on the wrong problem.
storyboard.staging: Hourglass icon, host slumped in worry: years lost on the wrong question.

storyboard.claim: Famous creators say they think best while alone, in the shower or on a walk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host thinking in a bare room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the counterpoint to the social claim.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists shaving, dog walks and traffic as solitary settings.
storyboard.staging: Host thinking alone: the solitary setting the creators describe.

storyboard.claim: The shower story seems to have no colleagues in it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host raising a skeptical eyebrow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Challenges the solitary-shower image.
storyboard.addedInformation: Asks the question the social theory has to answer.
storyboard.staging: Host with a skeptical smirk: the question the colleagues would answer.

storyboard.claim: Incubation is the background process; insight is the sudden moment it surfaces.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host explaining two stages of thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the vocabulary for the shower moment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Defines the two stages the next beats connect to the social work.
storyboard.staging: Host explaining two stages: the terms carry the claim.

storyboard.claim: The solo spark comes from earlier collisions with the field and its data.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow: field friction, data loaded, solo spark.
storyboard.onScreenText: Field friction, data loaded, solo spark
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the insight as the product of social work.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the causal chain from social friction to the spark.
storyboard.staging: Diagram beat: the chain of cause and effect carries the claim.

storyboard.claim: Deep focus blocks the conscious mind, so the answer must come later.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host thinking, head bowed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the focus that comes before the shower.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says focus is what stops the conscious mind from solving.
storyboard.staging: Host thinking under pressure: focus blocks the answer.

storyboard.claim: Relaxed attention lets the subconscious connect ideas in the background.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host walking, relaxed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the shower or walk lets the answer through.
storyboard.addedInformation: Relaxed attention is the state, not a source of ideas.
storyboard.staging: Host walking: the relaxed state the narration describes.

storyboard.claim: The dots were collected through public social interaction and study.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host talking beside the gatekeeper in the panel room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reverses the solitary image: the material came from others.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the subconscious connections back to the field.
storyboard.staging: Two people side by side: the public exchange that gathers the dots.

storyboard.claim: The shower does not create ideas; it only lets them surface.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host pointing away from the shower, rejecting it as a source.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the shower as the origin of ideas.
storyboard.addedInformation: The solitary spark is delayed friction from the field.
storyboard.staging: Host pointing away, rejecting the shower as a source: strike.

storyboard.claim: New problems rarely fit existing corporate jobs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host talking about the corporate box.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the solitary spark to the career it creates.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the corporate box as the normal frame that new problems break.
storyboard.staging: Host talking: new problems break the standard job frame.

storyboard.claim: True creators often must invent their own career path.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A road icon beside the host pointing down an unmarked path.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the corporate box does not fit.
storyboard.addedInformation: The road is a path that has to be built from nothing.
storyboard.staging: Road icon, host pointing: the path must be invented.

callout.text: LINUS PAULING AT SEVEN YEARS OLD

storyboard.claim: Linus Pauling was a seven-year-old in his father's drugstore back room.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boy in a faded hoodie in a back room of a drugstore.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the Pauling example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the child whose curiosity grew into a career.
storyboard.staging: Boy idling in the back room: the setting is the story.

storyboard.claim: He mixes two different powders in the jars of chemicals.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boy reaching to mix powders in a cup.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the experiment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the act of mixing: the experiment is the subject.
storyboard.staging: Boy reaching with a cup of powder: the mixing is the action.

storyboard.claim: A totally new third substance is created in front of him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boy with a cup, surprised by the result.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the mixing with the reaction.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fizzing reaction is the surprise: a new substance.
storyboard.staging: Boy surprised with the cup: the reaction is new.

storyboard.claim: His eyes go wide with awe at the reaction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boy holding the cup, eyes wide.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows his reaction to the new substance.
storyboard.addedInformation: Awe, the first sign of the lifelong drive.
storyboard.staging: Boy holding the cup with wide eyes: the awe is the claim.

storyboard.claim: The realization that matter can be transformed by invisible rules.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boy holding the cup with a delighted face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the awe into an idea.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the invisible rules as the thing he discovers.
storyboard.staging: Boy delighted with the cup: the realization of invisible rules.

storyboard.claim: That sense of wonder drove him for the next eighty years.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boy thinking, the same figure as the lifelong thread.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the child to the lifelong drive.
storyboard.addedInformation: Time span is the claim, the figure stands for the lifetime.
storyboard.staging: Boy thinking: the wonder lasting a lifetime.

storyboard.claim: Pauling won two Nobel prizes, which is very rare.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy icon beside the host reacting to the rarity.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the outcome of the eighty years.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trophy stands for the Nobel prize, not for a specific achievement.
storyboard.staging: Trophy icon, host surprised: rare recognition.

callout.text: A job that did not exist

storyboard.claim: You must carve out a job description that did not exist before.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host talking about a job that is not on any form.
storyboard.onScreenText: A job that did not exist
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the career-path point with the Pauling example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the corporate ladder cannot produce historically creative work.
storyboard.staging: Host talking: the job is invented, not climbed.

storyboard.claim: Rosalyn Yalow won a Nobel for the radioimmunoassay technique.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host holding a photo of the scientist.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the second example, Yalow.
storyboard.addedInformation: The photo marks her as the named person in the story.
storyboard.staging: Host holding a photo: the named scientist is the subject.

callout.text: Half a sugar lump in a lake

storyboard.claim: Finding tiny amounts of hormones is nearly impossible.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host with a magnifier, thinking about a tiny speck in a lake.
storyboard.onScreenText: Half a sugar lump in a lake
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the difficulty of the technique.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sugar-in-a-lake image makes the scale of the problem concrete.
storyboard.staging: Host with a magnifier: the search for a tiny speck.

storyboard.claim: Radioactive tags are attached to a known hormone, then mixed with antibodies and blood.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host holding a cup with tagged material.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the technique works.
storyboard.addedInformation: Describes the steps: tag, mix, add the blood sample.
storyboard.staging: Host holding a cup: the tagged mixture is the method.

storyboard.claim: Measuring the radioactive glow reveals tiny hormone amounts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host pointing at a glow with a magnifier.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the measurement step.
storyboard.addedInformation: The glow is the measurement: brightness gives the amount.
storyboard.staging: Host pointing with a happy face: the glow is the answer.

storyboard.claim: Yalow and her partner did not simply pass the technique on and leave.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host talking, neutral.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to what they did next.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says they stayed to see the bigger use, not a finished hand-off.
storyboard.staging: Host talking: the narration carries the contrast.

storyboard.claim: They realised the technique could measure insulin, vitamins and more.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host pointing, surprised, at the wider uses.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the broader use of the technique.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists insulin and vitamins as the new targets.
storyboard.staging: Host surprised, pointing outward: the wider use is the discovery.

storyboard.claim: They effectively created the entirely new field of modern medicine.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A medical icon beside the celebrating host.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the Yalow example on the field she created.
storyboard.addedInformation: The field is what they built, not a single result.
storyboard.staging: Medical icon, host celebrating: the field is the achievement.
